claims: The annual Chicago River dyeing is a 64-year St. Patrick's Day tradition.
The annual Chicago River dyeing takes place on March 14, 2026, around 10 AM, according to Instagram posts by colinbphoto and Block Club Chicago.
The annual Chicago River dyeing turns the water a bright emerald green, according to Instagram posts by colinbphoto and Block Club Chicago.
The Chicago River dyeing is led by the Chicago Plumbers Union Local 130.
About 40 pounds of eco-friendly, vegetable-based powder is used in the Chicago River dyeing.
The powder used in the Chicago River dyeing appears orange in the boat but turns green upon hitting the water.
The best viewing for the Chicago River dyeing is between Michigan Avenue and Columbus Drive, according to NBC 5 Chicago.
The Chicago River dyeing event occurred at 10 AM on Saturday, March 14, 2026.
Top locations to watch the Chicago River dyeing include the Chicago River between State and Columbus, and along Upper Wacker Drive, according to Choose Chicago and NBC 5 Chicago.
Plumbers Union Local 130 uses boats to spray the environmentally friendly, secret-formula dye into the water for the Chicago River dyeing.
The Chicago River dyeing tradition started in 1962, according to Block Club Chicago and USA Today.
The vibrant green color of the Chicago River dyeing typically lasts for a few hours to a couple of days.
The Chicago River dyeing event is usually broadcast live on local news stations and streamed online, according to NBC 5 Chicago.
The Chicago River dyeing serves as the official kickoff for Chicago's St. Patrick's Day celebrations, according to FOX 32 Chicago.
Chicago's St. Patrick's Day celebrations include the downtown parade immediately following the Chicago River dyeing, according to FOX 32 Chicago.
